text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Mississippi. January, eighteen sixty-nine. Four years since freedom came down the road.
subtitle: Mississippi. January, eighteen sixty-nine. Four years since freedom came down the road.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Five of us in a one-room cabin. Hannah. Our girl Lucy, ten. Our boy Sam, six. And my mother, Ruth.
subtitle: Five of us in a one-room cabin. Hannah. Our girl Lucy, ten. Our boy Sam, six. And my mother, Ruth.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] In sixty-five, folks said the bottom rail was on top. I'll believe it when I'm holding a deed.
subtitle: In sixty-five, folks said the bottom rail was on top. I'll believe it when I'm holding a deed.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Mr. Holliday has land and nobody to work it. I have two hands, a family, and nothing else.
subtitle: Mr. Holliday has land and nobody to work it. I have two hands, a family, and nothing else.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] So this morning I walk up to the big house to make my mark.
subtitle: So this morning I walk up to the big house to make my mark.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah says make him read every word. I can't read a one of them. He knows that.
subtitle: Hannah says make him read every word. I can't read a one of them. He knows that.

text_for_elevenlabs: Sit down, Robert. I'll read it, you listen. Saves us both some time.
subtitle: Sit down, Robert. I'll read it, you listen. Saves us both some time.

text_for_elevenlabs: For every thirty acres, I'll provide a mule team, plow, and farming tools. You can have half of the cotton and corn you grow.
subtitle: For every thirty acres, I'll provide a mule team, plow, and farming tools. You can have half of the cotton and corn you grow.
notes: Adapted from the 1882 Grimes contract (SHEG). Brisk and flat, a man who has read this many times.

text_for_elevenlabs: Nothing can be sold from your crop until my rent is all paid, and all amounts you owe me are paid in full.
subtitle: Nothing can be sold from your crop until my rent is all paid, and all amounts you owe me are paid in full.

text_for_elevenlabs: The sale of your part of the cotton to be made by me, when and where I choose to sell, and after taking all you owe me.
subtitle: The sale of your part of the cotton to be made by me, when and where I choose to sell, and after taking all you owe me.

text_for_elevenlabs: Fifteen acres. Five in corn, no more. Your account's at my commissary. Ten percent on anything you carry over. Make your mark right there.
subtitle: Fifteen acres. Five in corn, no more. Your account's at my commissary. Ten percent on anything you carry over. Make your mark right there.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] He read it fast, like a grocery list. I caught 'half.' I caught 'all you owe me.'
subtitle: He read it fast, like a grocery list. I caught 'half.' I caught 'all you owe me.'

text_for_elevenlabs: [respectfully] Yes, sir.
subtitle: Yes, sir.
when: As the student makes the mark

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] My mark. An X. Lucy is going to learn to write our name.
subtitle: My mark. An X. Lucy is going to learn to write our name.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Spring comes early. First stop, the commissary. Seed, and meat, meal, and molasses on account.
subtitle: Spring comes early. First stop, the commissary. Seed, and meat, meal, and molasses on account.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Only store for nine miles. Whatever we take, he writes down. Hannah ties a knot.
subtitle: Only store for nine miles. Whatever we take, he writes down. Hannah ties a knot.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Fifteen acres. More than I ever worked for myself. Not one of them mine.
subtitle: Fifteen acres. More than I ever worked for myself. Not one of them mine.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Cotton pays at settling time. Corn feeds us all year. Hannah wants corn. Mr. Holliday wants cotton.
subtitle: Cotton pays at settling time. Corn feeds us all year. Hannah wants corn. Mr. Holliday wants cotton.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Walk the rows. Hannah and the children come behind me with the seed.
subtitle: Walk the rows. Hannah and the children come behind me with the seed.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Field's in. Now it's up to the rain, the Lord, and the price.
subtitle: Field's in. Now it's up to the rain, the Lord, and the price.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] By June we chop cotton. By the Fourth of July it's laid by. Home for supper.
subtitle: By June we chop cotton. By the Fourth of July it's laid by. Home for supper.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] September. The bolls are open. Picking time runs till frost.
subtitle: September. The bolls are open. Picking time runs till frost.
when: Walk to the field in the fall

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Every row we walk is money. Whose money, we'll find out at Christmas.
subtitle: Every row we walk is money. Whose money, we'll find out at Christmas.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The bales are tied and loaded. His gin. His scale. His book.
subtitle: The bales are tied and loaded. His gin. His scale. His book.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] His man reads the needle and writes it down. I watch the needle. I can read a needle.
subtitle: His man reads the needle and writes it down. I watch the needle. I can read a needle.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] First of December, I voted. First time in my life. A week later, I walk up the hill to settle.
subtitle: First of December, I voted. First time in my life. A week later, I walk up the hill to settle.
notes: Mississippi ratified its new constitution November 30 to December 1, 1869.

text_for_elevenlabs: Come on up, Robert. I've got your number right here.
subtitle: Come on up, Robert. I've got your number right here.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Our first year free and settled. Whatever that number is, it's ours to carry.
subtitle: Our first year free and settled. Whatever that number is, it's ours to carry.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] February, eighteen seventy. The Fifteenth Amendment. I already voted once. Now the Constitution says no state can take it from me because of my color.
subtitle: February, eighteen seventy. The Fifteenth Amendment. I already voted once. Now the Constitution says no state can take it from me because of my color.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Voteless. That word gets crossed out. Landless. That one stays.
subtitle: Voteless. That word gets crossed out. Landless. That one stays.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Same month, a Black man from Mississippi, Hiram Revels, takes a seat in the United States Senate. Now watch, I tell Hannah. Now watch.
subtitle: Same month, a Black man from Mississippi, Hiram Revels, takes a seat in the United States Senate. Now watch, I tell Hannah. Now watch.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] New year, same road. I tell Hannah this is the year we come out ahead. I say that every spring.
subtitle: New year, same road. I tell Hannah this is the year we come out ahead. I say that every spring.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah asks what the flour costs. The clerk says, 'Same as always,' and writes it down.
subtitle: Hannah asks what the flour costs. The clerk says, 'Same as always,' and writes it down.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy walks beside me. She says the church is starting a school. She wants to go.
subtitle: Lucy walks beside me. She says the church is starting a school. She wants to go.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Cotton was down last fall. Corn doesn't care about New York.
subtitle: Cotton was down last fall. Corn doesn't care about New York.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Sam drags his own sack this year. Taller every spring.
subtitle: Sam drags his own sack this year. Taller every spring.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Mother told me tonight my father would have walked ten miles to vote. They sold him to Alabama when I was six.
subtitle: Mother told me tonight my father would have walked ten miles to vote. They sold him to Alabama when I was six.
notes: Review flag: Papa's memory of his father being sold. Brief and offstage, per the house rule.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Picking time. Sam fills his first whole sack. He's prouder of it than anything.
subtitle: Picking time. Sam fills his first whole sack. He's prouder of it than anything.
when: Walk to the field in the fall

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah sings in the next row. Sam sings louder, and wrong. Lucy laughs.
subtitle: Hannah sings in the next row. Sam sings louder, and wrong. Lucy laughs.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Loaded. I count the bales twice. I want to know the number before he tells me.
subtitle: Loaded. I count the bales twice. I want to know the number before he tells me.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The needle stops. I hold that number in my head all the way up the hill.
subtitle: The needle stops. I hold that number in my head all the way up the hill.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I put on my good shirt. Hannah walks up with me.
subtitle: I put on my good shirt. Hannah walks up with me.

text_for_elevenlabs: Evening, Robert. Cotton's down this year. Nothing I can do about New York.
subtitle: Evening, Robert. Cotton's down this year. Nothing I can do about New York.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Walking home, I don't say much. I never do after settling.
subtitle: Walking home, I don't say much. I never do after settling.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Word came from Meridian. A fire, a trial, then shooting in the courthouse. Our people, mostly.
subtitle: Word came from Meridian. A fire, a trial, then shooting in the courthouse. Our people, mostly.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah keeps her own count now. One knot for every dollar he writes.
subtitle: Hannah keeps her own count now. One knot for every dollar he writes.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Mother says the land doesn't care whose name is on it. It just wants working.
subtitle: Mother says the land doesn't care whose name is on it. It just wants working.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Every acre of corn is a little less owed. Every acre of cotton is a little more hope.
subtitle: Every acre of corn is a little less owed. Every acre of cotton is a little more hope.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The preacher's wife is teaching Lucy her letters on Sundays. She writes them in the dirt between rows.
subtitle: The preacher's wife is teaching Lucy her letters on Sundays. She writes them in the dirt between rows.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Laid by. Evenings on the porch, I count on my fingers. Hannah counts on her string.
subtitle: Laid by. Evenings on the porch, I count on my fingers. Hannah counts on her string.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah watches the wagon fill. She doesn't say anything. She's counting.
subtitle: Hannah watches the wagon fill. She doesn't say anything. She's counting.
when: Walk to the field in the fall

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I know what a wagon of cotton weighs. My back knows.
subtitle: I know what a wagon of cotton weighs. My back knows.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah walks beside the wagon this year. She wants to see the needle too.
subtitle: Hannah walks beside the wagon this year. She wants to see the needle too.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah leans close and whispers it. She's right. And there's not a thing I can say.
subtitle: Hannah leans close and whispers it. She's right. And there's not a thing I can say.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Up the hill. He won't look up from his book. He never does.
subtitle: Up the hill. He won't look up from his book. He never does.

text_for_elevenlabs: Robert. Let's see where you stand.
subtitle: Robert. Let's see where you stand.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah unties her string on the table tonight. We count the knots together. His book has more.
subtitle: Hannah unties her string on the table tonight. We count the knots together. His book has more.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Election year. Grant is running again. Men argue about it on every porch.
subtitle: Election year. Grant is running again. Men argue about it on every porch.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] New shoes in the commissary window. Hannah walks right past them.
subtitle: New shoes in the commissary window. Hannah walks right past them.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Mother can't walk out to the field this year. Her knees won't carry her.
subtitle: Mother can't walk out to the field this year. Her knees won't carry her.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah says plant more corn. Owe less. Eat. She's not wrong. She's never wrong.
subtitle: Hannah says plant more corn. Owe less. Eat. She's not wrong. She's never wrong.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Sam asks if his grandmother is coming out today. Not today, son.
subtitle: Sam asks if his grandmother is coming out today. Not today, son.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy read me the sign on the store today. Every letter. My daughter reads.
subtitle: Lucy read me the sign on the store today. Every letter. My daughter reads.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Long picking this year. We sing to keep the rows even.
subtitle: Long picking this year. We sing to keep the rows even.
when: Walk to the field in the fall

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah says we could leave. Leave owing, and he takes the mule, the crop, the stove. Then where?
subtitle: Hannah says we could leave. Leave owing, and he takes the mule, the crop, the stove. Then where?

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Same wagon. Same road. Same scale.
subtitle: Same wagon. Same road. Same scale.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Four years of that needle. It never once comes out on my side.
subtitle: Four years of that needle. It never once comes out on my side.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Four Christmases on that porch. I could find it in the dark.
subtitle: Four Christmases on that porch. I could find it in the dark.

text_for_elevenlabs: Another year, Robert. You're a good worker. I'd hate to lose you.
subtitle: Another year, Robert. You're a good worker. I'd hate to lose you.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] 'I'd hate to lose you.' He means it. That's the worst part.
subtitle: 'I'd hate to lose you.' He means it. That's the worst part.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah counts every coin twice this spring. Something's coming. We can all feel it.
subtitle: Hannah counts every coin twice this spring. Something's coming. We can all feel it.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The prices on the shelf haven't changed. They never do.
subtitle: The prices on the shelf haven't changed. They never do.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] One more good year. That's all we need. I've said that before.
subtitle: One more good year. That's all we need. I've said that before.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Corn or cotton. Five years of the same question, and I still don't know the right answer.
subtitle: Corn or cotton. Five years of the same question, and I still don't know the right answer.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy asks, when we have our own land, can she name the mule?
subtitle: Lucy asks, when we have our own land, can she name the mule?

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hard rain this summer, and fever down in Grenada and Vicksburg. We keep the children close.
subtitle: Hard rain this summer, and fever down in Grenada and Vicksburg. We keep the children close.
when: Walk home to the cabin (no event card this summer)
notes: Yellow fever reached Grenada and frightened Vicksburg in 1873.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Best crop we ever grew.
subtitle: Best crop we ever grew.
when: Arriving at the field in the fall, just before the Panic cutscene

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Best crop we ever grew, and nobody wants to buy it.
subtitle: Best crop we ever grew, and nobody wants to buy it.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I lead the wagon slow. No hurry to hear it.
subtitle: I lead the wagon slow. No hurry to hear it.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The needle stops. It doesn't matter now. The price was decided in New York.
subtitle: The needle stops. It doesn't matter now. The price was decided in New York.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy follows me up the hill this time and stands on the step to listen.
subtitle: Lucy follows me up the hill this time and stands on the step to listen.

text_for_elevenlabs: Sit down, Robert. Bad year for everybody. Even me.
subtitle: Sit down, Robert. Bad year for everybody. Even me.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] September, eighteen seventy-three. A bank in New York fails, and then the whole country seems to.
subtitle: September, eighteen seventy-three. A bank in New York fails, and then the whole country seems to.
when: Cutscene in the fall of 1873, before the harvest (moved from spring: the Panic began September 18)

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] Cotton falls to sixty dollars a bale. We grew it all year at the old price.
subtitle: Cotton falls to sixty dollars a bale. We grew it all year at the old price.
when: Cutscene in the fall of 1873, before the harvest (moved from spring: the Panic began September 18)

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] No shoes this year. We'll make do. We always make do.
subtitle: No shoes this year. We'll make do. We always make do.
when: After the student picks a basket

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] That should see us through, if nothing goes wrong.
subtitle: That should see us through, if nothing goes wrong.
when: After the student picks a basket

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Medicine on the shelf. Hannah will sleep better. So will I.
subtitle: Medicine on the shelf. Hannah will sleep better. So will I.
when: After the student picks a basket

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Five acres of corn. That's all the contract allows. He wants cotton.
subtitle: Five acres of corn. That's all the contract allows. He wants cotton.
when: Trying to plant a sixth acre of corn

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] That's enough. The family will finish the rest.
subtitle: That's enough. The family will finish the rest.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah and the children will bring in the rest.
subtitle: Hannah and the children will bring in the rest.

text_for_elevenlabs: Well. Your share comes out ahead this year. Don't spend it all in one place.
subtitle: Well. Your share comes out ahead this year. Don't spend it all in one place.

text_for_elevenlabs: Comes out even. Nothing owed, nothing coming.
subtitle: Comes out even. Nothing owed, nothing coming.

text_for_elevenlabs: You come up short. I'll carry it over to next year. Ten percent, same as always.
subtitle: You come up short. I'll carry it over to next year. Ten percent, same as always.
when: In debt for the first time

text_for_elevenlabs: Short again, Robert. I'll carry it. I always do.
subtitle: Short again, Robert. I'll carry it. I always do.

text_for_elevenlabs: I hear you went to town on Election Day. I'll keep your share for the trouble. Be gone by New Year's.
subtitle: I hear you went to town on Election Day. I'll keep your share for the trouble. Be gone by New Year's.
when: Voted, and the 1-in-4 eviction comes up

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Ahead. Say it again. Ahead. Hannah squeezes my hand all the way down the hill.
subtitle: Ahead. Say it again. Ahead. Hannah squeezes my hand all the way down the hill.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Even. A whole year of work, and we're right where we started.
subtitle: Even. A whole year of work, and we're right where we started.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Short. Hannah's string says we're closer than that. I keep my mouth shut.
subtitle: Short. Hannah's string says we're closer than that. I keep my mouth shut.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Every year we work harder, and every year we owe more.
subtitle: Every year we work harder, and every year we owe more.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Put off the place. We load the wagon. We've moved before. We'll move again.
subtitle: Put off the place. We load the wagon. We've moved before. We'll move again.

text_for_elevenlabs: [respectfully] Yes, sir.
subtitle: Yes, sir.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] A man asking to see the books. On this porch. Hannah is holding her breath.
subtitle: A man asking to see the books. On this porch. Hannah is holding her breath.

text_for_elevenlabs: [carefully] Sir... I'd like to see the books.
subtitle: Sir... I'd like to see the books.

text_for_elevenlabs: You'd call me a liar on my own porch? Your share stays with me. Be gone by New Year's.
subtitle: You'd call me a liar on my own porch? Your share stays with me. Be gone by New Year's.

text_for_elevenlabs: That's the time price. Goods on credit cost more than cash. Always have. It's in the contract.
subtitle: That's the time price. Goods on credit cost more than cash. Always have. It's in the contract.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Forty cents on every dollar, just for waiting till Christmas.
subtitle: Forty cents on every dollar, just for waiting till Christmas.

text_for_elevenlabs: The scale is the scale, Robert. You want to weigh your own cotton, buy your own gin.
subtitle: The scale is the scale, Robert. You want to weigh your own cotton, buy your own gin.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] So the wagon did weigh more. Hannah was right.
subtitle: So the wagon did weigh more. Hannah was right.

text_for_elevenlabs: Ten, twenty-five... interest is interest. You want land of your own someday or not?
subtitle: Ten, twenty-five... interest is interest. You want land of your own someday or not?

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Twenty-five percent. He said ten. He said it to my face.
subtitle: Twenty-five percent. He said ten. He said it to my face.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] If we leave owing, his lien takes the crop, the mule, everything we can't carry. No planter in the county will sign me.
subtitle: If we leave owing, his lien takes the crop, the mule, everything we can't carry. No planter in the county will sign me.
when: Choosing to leave while in debt

text_for_elevenlabs: Suit yourself. Plenty of men want this place.
subtitle: Suit yourself. Plenty of men want this place.

text_for_elevenlabs: Renting. Well. You've got the mule and the money. I won't stand in your way.
subtitle: Renting. Well. You've got the mule and the money. I won't stand in your way.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Rain at planting, and dry at picking. The cotton stands tall. A good year, if the price holds.
subtitle: Rain at planting, and dry at picking. The cotton stands tall. A good year, if the price holds.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] No rain from June to August. The bolls come in small and hard. I can hear them rattle.
subtitle: No rain from June to August. The bolls come in small and hard. I can hear them rattle.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The river comes up over the low fields. It takes the corn patch and some of the cotton.
subtitle: The river comes up over the low fields. It takes the corn patch and some of the cotton.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Old Jack lies down in his stall and doesn't get up. The mule was in my hands, so the cost goes in his book.
subtitle: Old Jack lies down in his stall and doesn't get up. The mule was in my hands, so the cost goes in his book.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Our own mule, lying in the stall. Sixty dollars of savings. Back to half shares.
subtitle: Our own mule, lying in the stall. Sixty dollars of savings. Back to half shares.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Sam takes the chills and fever in July. Hannah sits up with him nine nights. We're a pair of hands short.
subtitle: Sam takes the chills and fever in July. Hannah sits up with him nine nights. We're a pair of hands short.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Sam takes the chills and fever. We have medicine on the shelf this time. Thank God for that.
subtitle: Sam takes the chills and fever. We have medicine on the shelf this time. Thank God for that.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The church is starting a school for children. Lucy wants to go. That's one less pair of hands in the field.
subtitle: The church is starting a school for children. Lucy wants to go. That's one less pair of hands in the field.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The new public school opens, free. But it runs in the same months as chopping and picking.
subtitle: The new public school opens, free. But it runs in the same months as chopping and picking.
notes: Mississippi's school law of July 1870 made public schools free; terms were about four months.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy goes to school. The rows are a little longer without her. I don't mind the walk.
subtitle: Lucy goes to school. The rows are a little longer without her. I don't mind the walk.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Lucy stays in the field. She keeps asking. I keep saying next year.
subtitle: Lucy stays in the field. She keeps asking. I keep saying next year.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Election Day. I can vote, and he knows it. He says a man who votes against him can find another place to live.
subtitle: Election Day. I can vote, and he knows it. He says a man who votes against him can find another place to live.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I walk to town and vote. Nobody says a word to me on the road home. Nobody needs to.
subtitle: I walk to town and vote. Nobody says a word to me on the road home. Nobody needs to.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I stay home. I don't say a word all day. Neither does Hannah.
subtitle: I stay home. I don't say a word all day. Neither does Hannah.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] A neighbor moving west to Texas will sell his mule for sixty dollars, cash money.
subtitle: A neighbor moving west to Texas will sell his mule for sixty dollars, cash money.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I count out sixty dollars. The mule is ours. Two-thirds of the crop from now on.
subtitle: I count out sixty dollars. The mule is ours. Two-thirds of the crop from now on.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] I watch the mule go down the road. Maybe next year.
subtitle: I watch the mule go down the road. Maybe next year.
when: Summer, at the cabin. Papa voices the card; the effect and the Did You Know note stay on screen as text.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Sixty dollars cash. We don't have it. Not close.
subtitle: Sixty dollars cash. We don't have it. Not close.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Mother's garden comes in thick. Hannah walks to town on Saturday with eggs and greens.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] She comes home with fifteen dollars in her apron. Cash. Ours.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] The garden's too small this year to spare anything for town.
subtitle: The garden's too small this year to spare anything for town.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Word of masked men riding at night, two farms over. I bar the door and sit up with the lamp out.
subtitle: Word of masked men riding at night, two farms over. I bar the door and sit up with the lamp out.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Nobody in town will name a price. The buyers say wait. The planter says sell.
subtitle: Nobody in town will name a price. The buyers say wait. The planter says sell.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] 'Next year,' he says. 'Cotton will come back.' 'Yes, sir,' I say.
subtitle: 'Next year,' he says. 'Cotton will come back.' 'Yes, sir,' I say.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] We plant again the next spring, and the spring after that. The rows stay the same. Only the number in his book gets bigger.
subtitle: We plant again the next spring, and the spring after that. The rows stay the same. Only the number in his book gets bigger.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] January. We load the wagon and drive our own mule down the road. The land still isn't ours. But the crop will be.
subtitle: January. We load the wagon and drive our own mule down the road. The land still isn't ours. But the crop will be.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] That fall I sell our cotton myself. I read the price off the board in town, and I count the money twice.
subtitle: That fall I sell our cotton myself. I read the price off the board in town, and I count the money twice.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] We leave at night, owing. We make it as far as the county line.
subtitle: We leave at night, owing. We make it as far as the county line.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] His lien takes the crop, the mule, even Hannah's stove. The justice of the peace sides with him.
subtitle: His lien takes the crop, the mule, even Hannah's stove. The justice of the peace sides with him.

text_for_elevenlabs: [thoughtful] No planter in the county will sign a man who walked off owing. I hire out by the day, to whoever will have me.
subtitle: No planter in the county will sign a man who walked off owing. I hire out by the day, to whoever will have me.

text_for_elevenlabs: [quietly] Hannah's string was right. Now see for yourself.
subtitle: Hannah's string was right. Now see for yourself.

text_for_elevenlabs: Get on back to work, Robert. We'll settle up at Christmas.
subtitle: Get on back to work, Robert. We'll settle up at Christmas.
